results.summary: Closed-loop and demo days were 'confirmed' by construction. compute_day now runs verify._control per minute: the override history (pause_control/force_native, to its end or to when it was cleared), the stored ticks by plans.active_at's rules (no plan made, the one in force past valid_until, a held or failed tick of a release; a guard hold or a failed solve keeps the plan before it in force), and at a closed-loop site's own edge (not the demo) the fallback_engaged/cleared and control_disabled/enabled events plus minutes with no telemetry row. At least 95 % of minutes under the plan is confirmed, at least 50 % partial (claims, share as fidelity_score), below that not_applied (claims nothing). The row carries `control` {in_force_share, released_min, no_plan_min, edge_fallback_min, edge_unheard_min}. Test helpers make_site and r6 _farm now store a standing plan (status superseded, 2015 to 2100), as a live site's ticks keep one.

_expected_start now restarts from the measured state (reset 'arm_change') on a day whose arm can be the plan (_plan_arm: not monitor, not a switchback native block) after a day the plan did not run (NOT_PLAN_ARM: recommendation_only, native_block, not_applied incl. control not in force, pending). Days the plan did not run still chain among themselves, and days withheld for data on read inputs keep the chain. _chain_starts and _chain_stale pass the same rule, so the restart is never reported stale. This amends round 6's DESIGN_LOG rule that a monitor or not-applied day keeps the chain (same reasoning as round 6's switchback restart); the r6 test that asserted chaining through a monitor day now covers a data-withheld day instead.

Measured first: replays counted a blank PV/load as zero, so 5 min of blank PV at noon over-claimed a farm day by Rs 663 and 15 min at a grid site by Rs 1,366 (load blanks under-claimed). verify._balance_fill now takes a blank PV or load from the minute's balance where the other flows were read; when both are blank, the net is exact and the PV is interpolated across the gap. The measured cases now move by Rs 0. A day whose load or daylight PV stays unread for more than 5 % of its minutes (REPLAY_UNREAD_MAX = GRID_UNRESOLVED_MAX) claims nothing (claim_withheld 'inputs_unread', row field inputs_unread_min), and the next day restarts under the existing rule. That cap also covers full logger dropouts, which the grid rule's 'seen' filter never counted. A PV blank at night (sun_position) is not an unread minute. The compute_day docstring now states what holds, including the known limit: a gap the balance cannot close and under 5 % is carried. The web app labels the new reason 'Claim withheld: load or solar data missing'. Separately, a seed-dependent r4 test's tolerance now allows for the 0.01 kWh rounding of the stored end energies (it failed on some draws).

Also covers pages-D-02 (a duplicate). verify.summary per baseline now has `claimed_rs` as the headline: the claiming days, less the provisional carry-over, plus the claimed MDI. New fields: `levers_claimed_rs` (the claim by lever, sums to claimed_rs); `saving_rs`/`levers` over every day whose saving is known (a withheld day's partial levers add to no total; before, golden 2,820 vs now 2,020); counts claiming_days, withheld_days and unclaimed_days. The fee check uses the same claim. Day rows: saving null on a withheld day, plus claimed_native_rs, claimed_tuned_rs, claims, not_claimed_reason, levers_kept, carry_over_provisional(_native_rs), control_share and inputs_unread_min. The web app's tiles and ledger now lead with the claim: 'Claimed saving against the native settings / a tuned table', lever rows from levers_claimed_rs, bold 'Claimed', then 'Every scored day, claimed or not'. Types and API_CONTRACT (Round 7 section) updated. Not done here: the export columns. routes_savings.savings_csv belongs to stage 2 savings-ui-crosscut, and reports.py's PDF headline, daily rows and CSV belong to alerts-reports; the per-day chart and days table are stage 2's. All the fields they need are now in the summary.
results.reason: The CSV and PDF columns (claimed, withheld reason) are in files other packages own: routes_savings.savings_csv (stage 2) and reports.py (alerts-reports). The API now carries every field they need.

results.summary: A claiming day's carry-over credit (its end gap at v_end) is now provisional while no later day has been scored: verify.summary leaves it out of claimed_rs and levers_claimed_rs.carry_over and reports it as carry_over_provisional_rs (per day: carry_over_provisional and carry_over_provisional_native_rs). Once the next day is scored, chained from it or restarting at a switchback block (plan 8.2's hand-over at v_end), the credit enters the claim. Golden: a claim of 2,000 with a last-day 300 credit reads 1,700 + 300 provisional, and 2,000 once day 5 is scored. The Faisalabad case (whole claim = last day's carry-over) now shows the realised figure with the carry-over apart. The fee check excludes it too. The web app shows 'Rs X of carry-over is provisional until the stored energy is used' under the tiles and a ledger row 'Carry-over still provisional (not in the claim)'. The off-grid farm's carry-over versus diesel (RYK) is round 6's chained ledger plus batch 2's carry-over items.

results.summary: Only a closed-loop site's edge now gets a plan. Below closed loop, plans.signed_message raises the new plans.NotClosedLoop: nothing is signed, sent or recorded in plan_messages, so a monitor site no longer shows 'Table writes today 1 of 3'. The key-only route GET /sites/:id/plans/current/message answers 409 not_closed_loop with a one-sentence reason, for example "The site's control tier is monitor, so no plan is sent to its edge: the plan is a recommendation". This covers its duplicate engine-plans-live-11. The gate also covers advisory_writes. Plan Part 2.3 sends signed plans to closed loop only. A signed release would make the edge restore native settings and overwrite the table a person keyed in, so a refusal is the safe answer. API_CONTRACT.md documents it under 'Round 7 (audit): control-edge'.

plans._guard can now refuse a plan, following Part 7.1 step 8 and R6 C2. A refused plan is held and the previous one stays in force. The guard returns the first rule broken: slot_floor_below_fallback (a slot floor under the fallback's minimum state of charge); replayed_soc_below_floor (with the grid up, the table replayed through the twin discharges the battery under the fallback floor; tolerance 5 points); unserved_in_outage (in forecast outages the replay leaves more critical load unserved than the plan did, by more than max(2 kWh, 5 % of the outage's critical energy)); mdi_cap_exceeded (see engine-plans-live-05); sheds_load_with_grid_up (the plan sheds load with the grid up that the replay serves from the grid); genset_slot_with_grid (a genset slot lies wholly in expected grid-present time at a site whose genset may not run beside the grid); export_not_allowed (an export slot at a connection with no export). The two old checks could never trip and are gone. A probe built 12 demo days with 3-hourly ticks (320 plans) on the new guard and held 1 plan, at Lahore, for real grid-up shedding. At a 2-point tolerance the floor rule had held 8 of 80 Lahore plans over a 2.1-point peak-shave dip, which is why the tolerance is 5 points. The web app names every new reason in words (GUARD_REASONS).
tests: frontend/src/features/plan/plan-held.test.tsx (Round 7: says the guard's reason ... in words)

results.summary: The guard now checks the plan's MDI cap (mdi_cap_exceeded). tick passes the solve's res to _guard, which is a one-line edit in tick, a function optimiser-plans owns. For each MDI block the guard takes the plan's own grid draw, adds back any load the plan sheds with the grid up (the meter reads that load), and adds the first block's minutes already elapsed, as the MILP row does. It refuses when the block mean exceeds res['M'] by more than 1 kW, using M2 after the billing month's end. This catches plans that meet their MDI only by shedding load the site cannot shed (the 02f1e98208e1 case). A single 15-minute step above the cap inside a 30-minute block whose mean is under it is not a new maximum demand, so it is not refused; a test covers this. That answers the per-step evidence (step 14, 962 kW against a 902 kW cap). A version that replayed the compiled table instead would have held about 25 % of the Faisalabad and Karachi demo plans. The cause there is a compile artefact: a non-charge slot's grid_cap is the maximum import of its span, which belongs to delivery-twin. Per Part 7.1 step 4, an MDI rise the device cannot prevent is reported as mdi_not_enforceable, not refused.

A plan past its valid_until is no longer in force. plans.current(site_id, now=None) returns None once valid_until has passed, and plans.active_at returns None for any instant at or after the plan's valid_until. held_info answers {reason: 'plan_expired', until: null, plan_id, since: valid_until}, and GET /plan passes 'since' through. signed_message returns None and the edge route answers 404 plan_expired. GET /control answers compiled: null, so no expired table is offered for keying in. The Plan page says 'The last plan ran out on <Pakistan date and time> ... the inverter runs its fallback, its own native settings', with a 'Read the last plan' button. The next good tick puts a plan in force again. Four existing test fixtures stored plans with valid_until equal to generated_at, or read today's clock for a historical tick; they were updated: test_fix_r3_api._plan_row (48 h), test_fix_savings._insert_plan (48 h) and test_engine (current(now=tick time)).
tests: frontend/src/features/plan/plan-held.test.tsx (Round 7: says the last plan ran out ...)

results.summary: Fixes engine-plans-live-01 too. On a grid-up step, U may now only take load beyond what the connection (G_max) and PV can carry: U_ub = max(0, L - G_max - PV). So the plan imports and prices the MDI rise instead of shedding real load. explain() names any unserved step 'unserved' with detail grid up, down or none (it used to say idle, self_consumption or mdi_cap). build_problem raises a VoLL saved below the horizon's dearest import price to that price, which closes the 'VoLL 0 makes floors and shortfall free' hole on the engine side. The web app's unserved sentence follows detail.grid. The audit's own repro (L[40:44] = 300, M0 = 100, E0 = 25) shed 194 kW with the grid up before the fix and sheds 0 after. A tick-level test checks a mill with a 100 to 300 kW afternoon hour: on the old code that plan shed 4 grid-up steps (Rs 95,880) and imported above its own cap on 25 steps; now it does neither.

Fixes engine-plans-live-04 and engine-plans-live-13 too. A grid charge that is not cheaper than the price its energy is used at, and that binding reserve rows hold, is now the new reason charge_for_reserve. Its detail carries rs_per_kwh, p, within_h, hours and kwh. p is the chance of an outage starting over the hold's whole window, not one step's p. hours is two steps behind an AMF panel, taken from solve's new R_steps. kwh is never above the usable band. charge_from_grid now carries use_t and use_rs_per_kwh. The web app sentence names the price paid and when the energy is used, and mentions a dearer price only when the use price really is dearer; 'while energy is cheaper' is gone. Peak buying itself is kept only where the reserve's priced shortfall pays for it ('priced and labelled'): below p = 0.01 there is no row and no peak grid charging (tested). The deeper causes of the inflated reserve (sigma, the AMF reserve, discharge power) are in later batches of this package.

Fixes engine-plans-live-14 too. A grid-up step with energy above the floor that neither charges nor discharges is now named from the solution's own figures, in this order:
- hold_for_outage: a reserve row binds from this step on, before the battery next charges or discharges. This also covers steps whose own p_start is under 0.01, so a held peak no longer flips with 'Wear > saving'. kwh is never above what the battery holds, p is the chance over the window, and hours is 0.5 h behind an AMF panel.
- save_for_later (new): the energy is discharged later, before the next charge. Detail use_t, use_rs_per_kwh, use_reason (for example the Karachi MDI case).
- wear_margin_too_small: only where putting the kWh back at the next charge leaves a positive gap below the wear cost. Detail gap_rs_per_kwh and wear_rs_per_kwh.
- terminal_value: nothing in the horizon refills or uses the energy.
At an off-grid site the battery 'carries the load' (carry_load, new) instead of 'carry_outage'. A tie-break of 0.002 Rs/kWh across the horizon, on grid-up steps only, discharges the earlier and charges the later of two equal steps. This removes the 80/0/80/0 'Peak discharge'/'Wear' alternation at one price; grid-down and off-grid costs are unchanged, so the farm's solve times are unaffected. On the web app, the hold sentence and the legend no longer say 'a likely outage': the legend gives the range of p its steps carry. Sentences were added for save_for_later, carry_load and wear with its figures. delivery.step_intents compiles save_for_later as a hold, like the no-flow reasons it replaces.

Every Mode A slot carries grid_cap_w = M, and the device shaves each instant above it, but the MDI rows only bounded each 30-minute block's mean. So a step could import above the cap (Karachi: 962 kW against 902), and charging ran 65.6/0/188.6/0 kW. Each grid-up step now gets its own row, G[t] + (Lhi[t] - L[t]) <= M (M2 after the month's end), under the upper load quantile as the block rows are. Planned import now stays at or under the plan's own cap step by step. Grid charging and peak shaving under a binding cap are smooth instead of alternating. The tick-level test also checks that no step imports above mdi_cap_kw.

results.summary: Backend: forecast.page() now also returns `past`: the 96 steps before belief_time with their 15-minute actuals (available PV, load, or 1 where the grid was down). It also carries the arrays of the issue held a day before over those steps (q05-q95 and cs for PV, quantiles and crit for load, p_down and p_start for outages). Its belief_time is None when no such issue exists. The actual computation moved into the shared helpers _actual15 and _past. Web app: withPast (forecast-words.ts, memoised in the panel) joins the past in front of the latest issue for the PV and load fans and the outage chart. The now line sits at belief_time between past and forecast, and a line under each chart says which issue the past shows. 'No actuals yet' shows only when neither part has a reading. An older backend without `past` renders as before.

With 3 to 6 fitted days, forecast.pv now keeps the prior's shape but moves its median from the month's climatology towards the site's median clearness, with weight days/7. The step to the empirical quantiles at 7 days stays small. Before the fix, the scaling term median(kn)/median(kn) was 1, so the prior was used unchanged. A mostly overcast 4-day site now forecasts a median below the prior's 0.89, and an all-clear site a median above it.

Both halves are fixed. (1) The 'last 7 days' figure now covers the last 7 calendar days in Pakistan time, with n7 days scored, instead of the last 7 scored rows. This is in scores() in the scoring commit, and the tiles show the n7 count. (2) The outage chart's p_start: p_start[i] is the chance an outage starts in step i+1, matching how optimise.py:314 holds the reserve at the end of step i. The new outageSeries (outage-probability-chart.tsx, used by both the Forecasts and Outages pages) now draws that series at t[i] + 15 minutes. The backend answer is unchanged.

results.summary: Fixed in both repositories. On the server, PUT /api/sites/:id, PUT /api/sites/:id/connection (with id) and PUT /api/sites/:id/assets/:role take an optional if_unchanged: the stored fields the form was based on, or null for a connection or asset when none was stored. If any of those fields has changed since, the save gets 409 site_changed. The sentence names the fields, `changed` lists their keys, and nothing is written. The check and the write share one write transaction, and the audit line is written in it. A save without if_unchanged works as before, so Site settings is unchanged. In the wizard, the form keeps the site as it last matched it (form.base, saved in the draft). A tab counts as complete only when its values are what the site holds, not when they match the draft's own snapshot. A resumed draft whose site changed since shows 'The site was changed after this draft last matched it, on tab A ...' with two buttons: 'Use the site's values' or 'Keep the draft's values'. A draft from before round 7 that differs from its site gets the same choice. Every save sends its part as if_unchanged. A 409 reads the site again and offers the same choice. Tab B's own per-asset Save and Remove buttons also check and move the base, one asset at a time, so another person's change to an asset this save did not write is still caught. Text in the site and asset bodies is trimmed the way the server stores it, so a saved tab compares equal to the site.
